refuted_candidates.title: The set-unwind-guard row with token=all writes one absolute minUsdcOut to every basket token, whatever each token's balance
refuted_candidates.reason:
The code facts are right, but the security claim does not hold. With token=all, publish-contracts/src/unwind-guard.ts:82 and :88-95 write the same minUsdcOut and maxLossBps to every active token, and the override floor math at contracts/lib/BasketSwapOps.sol:196 and :377-380 works as the scenario says. That behavior is documented on purpose (unwind-guard.ts:11 "all with the same values", publish-contracts/README.md:125, docs/operations/contract-release-runbooks.md:522).

Only ADMIN_ROLE writes the guard (contracts/vaults/BasketVault.sol:1338-1343). That role is the Safe acting through the 48h timelock. The Safe transaction description lists every per-token call with its values (publish-contracts/src/govern.ts:1353). The hot key still cannot choose its own price, so the ACL-5 property at docs/technical/smart-contract-invariants.md:142 still holds. In the scenario, the Safe signers chose a loose floor for one leg.

token=all also does not create the looseness. Any absolute floor goes loose as a holding grows or the price moves, whether it is set per token or with token=all. The docs accept this and tell the operator to run the row again. The stage 13 sitting sets the guard while the baskets still hold nothing, so every first floor is a guess for every leg. A wrong floor here needs an admin to misconfigure it on purpose, and the change is visible before signing. Refusing loose floors or printing TWAP values next to each floor is hardening, which the preamble rules out.

One real gap remains, at info level: the runbook asks for "one round per basket" (contract-release-runbooks.md:285). That steers rmPROTO toward token=all, where one value cannot match "size it from the current holding" for two legs of unequal value. This is a clarity issue in the docs, not an exploit.

refuted_candidates.title: CONFIRM=environment accepts any GitHub OIDC token from any robotmoney/* repository, fetched from an env-controlled URL, so the Environment reviewer sign-off can be replayed from a laptop
refuted_candidates.reason: The code path works as described, but there is no security impact. The only person who can pull it off already holds more power than the bypass gives. Each step checks out. publish-contracts/src/actions-proof.ts:146 accepts any repository under the robotmoney/ owner. actions-proof.ts:151 builds the expected sub from the token's own repository claim. actions-proof.ts:165-167 reads the token URL from the environment and accepts any https URL. cli.ts:497-499 fetches the proof once. runner.ts:494-498 then reuses it for every stage. So a genuine token relayed from an unprotected Environment in another org repo passes. The scenario needs one precondition: the laptop operator holds the 8453 deployer signer outside Actions, as env:signer or a keystore (signer.ts:73-107). That person already has full authority over every broadcast. First, the typed confirmation that CONFIRM=environment replaces reads both the 'Operator' and the 'Reviewer' answers from the same TTY (runner.ts:510-513, cli.ts:539). One person can type both, so the reviewer prompt never constrained the key holder. Second, the key holder can sign any transaction with cast and skip the tool entirely. The relay needs a pushed workflow with id-token: write, a live relay endpoint and deliberate env setup. That is strictly more work than typing the stage name twice. It also grants no asset, role or action the actor lacked. An accidental unattended run stays covered. A laptop with only GITHUB_ACTIONS=true has no request token and is refused (cli.ts:497, actions-proof.ts:51, floors.ts:119-123). Nobody sets up a relay by accident. The run is also not silent. cli.ts:499 logs run.actions_proof with the token's repository, workflow and run_id (actions-proof.ts:176-177), so the foreign repository appears in the run log. The 'reviewer sign-off' a relay replays guards nothing on a laptop. The Environment's real protection is gating the deploy secrets inside the devops job, and this code path never touches that. Pinning the repository and job_workflow_ref would tighten the proof against the doc claim at actions-proof.ts:2-4 ('it cannot mint a GitHub OIDC token'). That is hardening a process floor against its own key holder, not closing an exploit. At most it is a low-severity assertion-wording gap. It does not break any security boundary.

refuted_candidates.title: The verifier forces a non-zero absolute emergency-unwind floor on every leg, and the contract applies it as a hard minimum on the TWAP-healthy path, so emergencyUnwind reverts once a leg's value falls below the guard
refuted_candidates.reason:
The contract mechanics are real. On the healthy-TWAP path `_unwindLeg` uses max(twapFloor, configuredMin) (contracts/lib/BasketSwapOps.sol:370-377), and `emergencyUnwind` loops over every active leg in one transaction (BasketSwapOps.sol:171-175). The candidate's chain from tooling to a blocked lever breaks at two steps.

(1) The verifier does not require a floor of about half the leg value. It requires only minUsdcOut > 0 (publish-contracts/src/verify/index.ts:788-789, `zero = guards.filter(g => g.min === 0n)`). The tooling accepts min-usdc-out=1 with max-loss-bps=0 (unwind-guard.ts:63,70). With those values the healthy path behaves exactly as it did before D7. So the size of the floor is the operator's choice, not a verifier requirement.

(2) The lever does not stay blocked until a new 48 h round. When the plain unwind refuses a fill below the guard, the EMERGENCY key can call `emergencyUnwindWithOverride([token])` in the same incident (BasketVault.sol:1184-1191). Its floor is minUsdcOut*(MAX_BPS-maxLossBps)/MAX_BPS (BasketSwapOps.sol:194). The Safe chose that band, which can go up to 9999 bps. After that sale the leg's balance is 0, so `_unwindLeg` returns early at BasketSwapOps.sol:367 and a plain `emergencyUnwind` clears the other legs. The override reverts only if the operator picked a maxLossBps too tight for the drop, which is the declared loss cap working as intended.

The binding floor is also the documented design, not a composition failure. BasketVault.sol:1164-1166 calls the admin value "a secondary lower bound". smart-contract-invariants.md:142 says "the hot key can de-risk but cannot choose its own price". basket-vault-gap-report.md:122 says a distressed exit that must accept less than the guard uses `emergencyUnwindWithOverride`. The stale-floor risk is stated in unwind-guard.ts:7-8, publish-contracts/README.md:125 and contract-release-runbooks.md:522.

When the floor binds, the system fails safe: nothing sells below the Safe's floor. `pauseDeposits` (BasketVault.sol:1147), holder `redeem` (TWAP floors only, BasketSwapOps.sol:337-341) and `redeemInKind` are untouched by the guard. No attacker gets a new lever: spot manipulation can already block an unwind through twapFloor whatever configuredMin is.

What remains is a tooling usability gap. `token=all` applies one absolute value to legs of different sizes (unwind-guard.ts:11,82,90-94). govern never reads leg balances or TWAP values (no balanceOf or assetUsdcValue reads in govern.ts or unwind-guard.ts). The runbook says to rerun the row only "as the holding grows" (contract-release-runbooks.md:522), while unwind-guard.ts:8 says "as the holding changes". Under the rubric that is availability harm. It needs admin misconfiguration plus a market move, it fails safe, and no escalator applies. That makes it low at most, not medium.

refuted_candidates.title: The release gate's CI check queries whatever repository GITHUB_REPOSITORY names, and its remote-tag check trusts the checkout's origin
refuted_candidates.reason: The code facts are right, but they do not add up to a trust-root break. Both inputs the scenario changes belong to the operator who already holds the signing keys. The gate builds the check-sha-green env from i.env (publish-contracts/src/release-gate.ts:175-176). cli.ts:473 sets that env to `deps.env ?? process.env`, which is the operator's own shell. It is not the sheet and not any less-trusted input. The remote-tag check reads `origin` from the operator's local .git/config (release-tag.ts:54,60). The runbook already treats local clone state as operator-trusted and names code review plus the optional tag ruleset as the real controls (docs/operations/contract-release-runbooks.md:116-120 and 301: "That ref is LOCAL ... NOT provenance or review"). To pull off the scenario, the operator would have to set GITHUB_REPOSITORY to a fork, repoint origin to that fork, and make the fork emit forged check-runs with every required name. That same operator has much simpler bypasses. The CLI runs its gate from its own import location, not from coreDir. The clean-tree and HEAD checks (cli.ts:517-522) only cover the --core-dir checkout (cli.ts:364), so a patched cli.ts run from a second directory skips the gate entirely. The operator could also send transactions with the deployer key directly. The env var crosses no boundary. An accidental trigger needs three separate deliberate misconfigurations to line up, which is not plausible. The CI half is fail-closed by the candidate's own account. It also depends on the devops workflow, which nobody inspected. A core sha queried against the devops repo returns an API error, so the check exits 2 and the gate throws CI_NOT_GREEN (check-sha-green.ts:142,191-193; release-gate.ts:178-180). That is an availability concern at worst, not a security finding. The GITHUB_REPOSITORY passthrough was also added on purpose, in the original gate commit (a6fe712c, the contracts-freeze gate (1601)).

refuted_candidates.title: check-sha-green counts any check-run that has a required name, so a writer can fabricate a GREEN deploy sha
refuted_candidates.reason: The code facts are right, but the attack gives a writer nothing new, and the proposed fix would not stop that writer. check-sha-green.ts:51-55 matches only by name. fetchAllCheckRuns (check-sha-green.ts:138) keeps only name, status and conclusion. The `source` field (line 24) is never read. The scenario's attacker is a repository writer, and that writer already controls everything the gate trusts. First, the gate runs from the sha being deployed: release-gate.ts:29 spawns `bun scripts/ci/check-sha-green.ts` with cwd=coreDir, and cli.ts:517-518 refuses unless coreDir HEAD equals DEPLOY_SHA. So the gate script and required-checks.json both come from the tree the writer pushed. The runbook says this at contract-release-runbooks.md:108-109 and makes reviewing that diff the control. Second, dev is unprotected by an owner decision (ci-suites.md "Branch protection (won't fix)"). Push workflows run the workflow files in the pushed commit. So a writer can turn the suite jobs at A into no-ops and get a real GREEN from the github-actions app, from the correct workflow path, on a push to dev. The proposed fix (bind to app, workflow path and event) would accept that. CI green is therefore not a control against writers by design. For a final mainnet release the documented control is an external security review of the exact SHA, and contract-release-runbooks.md:172-178 says "a green CI run does not count". The scenario's no-run cases (a non-head commit of a multi-commit push, or a missing releases-* push) fail safe as MISSING (check-sha-green.ts:75, 99). The "Environment reviewers" step does not exist in this repo: no workflow under .github/workflows declares `environment:`. The filter=latest masking claim cannot be confirmed from the code, and the candidate itself marks it unverified. The only real difference is that forged check-runs do not show up in a diff. That makes this a low hardening note, not a high assertion forgery.

refuted_candidates.title: emergencyWithdraw alone still leaves an illiquid adapter counted in NAV, so early redeemers take full NAV from idle unless the hot key runs emergencyExcludeAdapter first
refuted_candidates.reason: The code works as the candidate says, but the scenario only happens when the trusted emergency key ignores a documented, accepted procedure, so it is not an exploitable value transfer. Only the emergency role can press emergencyWithdraw (contracts/RobotMoneyVault.sol:1087). With no emergency action, the illiquid adapter blocks any redeem larger than idle cash: the proportional pull reverts (contracts/lib/VaultAdapterOps.sol:344-356; contracts/test/RobotMoneyVault.t.sol:1318 expects VenueIlliquid). So no holder can start this alone. The protocol gives the hot key a lever that closes the gap: emergencyExcludeAdapter opens the exclusion record in one call (contracts/RobotMoneyVault.sol:1125, lib/VaultAdapterOps.sol:534-548). The required order is written into the NatSpec (contracts/RobotMoneyVault.sol:1118-1122), docs/technical/security-model.md:94, docs/technical/adapter-architecture.md:219-224 and docs/technical/smart-contracts.md:216-218. docs/audits.md:267 records this exact risk (FS-VLT-8) as accepted-with-rationale, with this order as the fix. The parity test (contracts/test/RobotMoneyVault.t.sol:1290) pins the safe order. Two points in the candidate are accurate: docs/operations has no emergency-withdraw runbook, and no CLI wraps the call. Those are gaps in operations docs and defence in depth. They are not a contract bug. The proposed auto-exclude on a failed drain is reasonable hardening, but nothing an unprivileged actor can trigger depends on it. If it were counted at all, it would be info: an admin must trigger it, and it repeats an already-accepted finding.

refuted_candidates.title: The rmpc export merges the dapp's per-address vault and router implementation pins into one flat list, and rmpc accepts any listed hash at any reached proxy
refuted_candidates.reason: The code shape is real but the scenario is blocked. rmpc's check_proxy_approved has no address binding (clients/rust-payment-client/src/upgrade.rs:222-250). The export unions the per-address pins (clients/dapp/src/components/AdminFlow.tsx:94-101, clients/dapp/src/lib/configExport.ts:148-156). The scenario needs one thing first: the timelock upgrading the rmUSDC proxy to the rmPROTO or router implementation. The only approved upgrade path refuses that. The upgrade-proxy row requires the target's runtime code to match the build artifact of that proxy's own contract (publish-contracts/src/upgrade-rows.ts:6-10 and :127). It also refuses a layout that moves any live storage variable (upgrade-rows.ts:133-147). Only the timelock can upgrade, behind a 48 hour public delay (contracts/lib/GovernedUpgrade.sol:148-152). The watchdog pages on every executed Upgraded event (services/watchdog/src/upgrade_events.rs:9-25). The dapp refuses the swapped implementation too, as the candidate itself says. That leaves one path: a compromised Safe quorum hand-crafting a raw timelock operation. Such a quorum could install code that drains all TVL, and rmpc would refuse it. So the flat list does not widen that attacker's power. It only limits their choice to reviewed code. The flat rmpc schema is also the documented operator contract. The release runbook gate on rmpc readiness (G4) has operators set proxy_implementation_hashes to the vault and router hashes together (docs/operations/contract-release-runbooks.md:651). BOOTSTRAP.md:263 says the same. So the export writes the same set operators were already told to write by hand. What remains is defense-in-depth against admin compromise. If counted at all, it is low: admin-only, with the dapp refusal and the watchdog page as other controls.

refuted_candidates.title: The 8453 build gate runs the build checkout's own check-sha-green.ts and required-checks.json with the operator's GitHub token
refuted_candidates.reason: The code path is real, but it is not an exploitable gap, and the proposed fix would not stop the scenario. The upgrade gate does run the build checkout's own script with the operator's token. That chain is cli.ts:713, govern.ts:796, build-provenance.ts:80, release-gate.ts:38 (cwd: i.coreDir) and release-gate.ts:184, and check-sha-green.ts:178 reads required-checks.json from its own directory. The attacker in the scenario is a writer who can land a commit and push a release tag. That writer already controls whether CI looks green at that commit, whichever copy of the script runs. Push and workflow_dispatch runs use the workflow files of the pushed ref (suite-01-02-forge-tests.yml:40-50). check-sha-green matches check runs by name only (check-sha-green.ts:51-57), with no app or workflow-path check. The same commit can rename no-op jobs to forge-unit-tests and every other required name. The deploy checkout's own script and list would then report green too. The token exposure adds no new power. The runbook (contract-release-runbooks.md:627) has the operator deploy the new implementation from that same checkout and build its out/ there. Forge reads that checkout's foundry.toml, which can point solc at any executable. So the operator already runs that checkout's code with the deployer key before govern starts. Reading the tagged sha's own list is also documented on purpose (contract-release-runbooks.md:108-109: review that file's diff before tagging). The controls that actually stop a bad implementation are the Safe threshold, the 48-hour timelock, the bytecode match to the build, and the watchdog alert on Upgraded. At most this is a low defense-in-depth note.

refuted_candidates.title: Router deposits are not bound to the weight vector the caller previewed: floors are positional, there is no deadline, and anyone can time the timelock execution of a new vector, so a signed floor can be applied to a different vault
refuted_candidates.reason: The scenario's key step does not happen through any production path. The govern tool builds every applyReceipt vector in registry order (publish-contracts/src/apply-receipt.ts:120-123, govern.ts:1859-1861). rmUSDC is registered first (contracts/script/DeployVaultRegistry.s.sol:150), so it is always leg 0. The tool would queue V2 as [rmUSDC 1000, rmPROTO 9000], not [rmPROTO 9000, rmUSDC 1000]. Default vectors use the same registry order (BasketVaultDeployBase.sol:192-214; DeployPortfolioRouter.s.sol:144-150). In that case leg 0 gets 10% of the USDC against a floor set for 100%, so the deposit reverts SlippageExceeded at PortfolioRouter.sol:1220. It fails safe. The only canonical path that reorders legs is the single-vault redeploy, which puts the new vault in the old vault's slot (redeploy-vault.ts:328) while registry order appends it (VaultRegistry.sol:254). That redeploy is refused on chain 8453 in production (redeploy-vault.ts:89-93). It also only applies to rmPROTO and never moves rmUSDC off leg 0. Producing the claimed reorder needs the Safe to hand-craft applyReceipt calldata outside its tooling, behind a public 48h timelock. That is an admin action, and the open executor only picks the block. Even then the user gets fair-value ERC-4626 shares in vaults governance approved. The basket's own realised-value floor still holds (BasketVault.sol:641). On-chain mechanics such as positional floors (PortfolioRouter.sol:1213), the length-only check (:1124), no deadline (:893, :919) and the open executor (DeployTimelock.s.sol:683) are as described. The routerPreview.ts:89 comment is loosely worded. Still, the claimed silent 100%-rmUSDC to 90%-basket outcome cannot be reached without admin misuse. Severity if it were real: low, since it needs admin action and has no loss beyond the basket slippage bound.

refuted_candidates.title: Incomplete round-1 fix: emergencyWithdraw still leaves an adapter whose drain failed priced in NAV, so drain-before-exclude repeats the early-redeemer haircut shift; the order lives only in NatSpec and technical docs
refuted_candidates.reason:
The mechanics reproduce. emergencyWithdrawAll (contracts/lib/VaultAdapterOps.sol:525-537) opens records only for entries that are already ineligible. _drain (:903-922) sets ok=false when withdraw reverts. The entry stays active and allowed with no record, so isCounted (:131-133) keeps it in totalAssets (contracts/RobotMoneyVault.sol:557-566). Alice can then redeem from idle at full NAV through the idle-first path (:777-805).

It is still not a vulnerability. The harm needs the trusted hot key (EMERGENCY_ROLE) to run the levers in the one order the docs forbid. The round-1 fix chose this operator ordering on purpose. docs/audits.md:267 marks FS-VLT-8 accepted-with-rationale: "Idle-first stays; the order is fixed instead: EMERGENCY_ROLE now excludes the adapter first". Four places state the order: docs/technical/security-model.md:94, docs/technical/smart-contracts.md:223-226, docs/technical/adapter-architecture.md:250-253 and the emergencyExcludeAdapter NatSpec (RobotMoneyVault.sol:1121-1126). The test RobotMoneyVault.t.sol:1457 pins it.

So the fix is complete for the scope it was given, not incomplete. The hot key can also close the window with one more call. The failed drain emits EmergencyWithdrawAdapterCalled(i, adapter, 0, false), and emergencyExcludeAdapter can follow straight away.

The proposed auto-exclude would be a design change with a trade-off. A transient withdraw revert would exclude the adapter until the 48 h ADMIN restore through setAdapterAllowed(true). That is speculative hardening, which the review contract rules out.

What remains real is an operations gap with no direct security impact. No docs/operations runbook and no publish-contracts command names emergencyExcludeAdapter or the exclude-then-drain order. The emergencyWithdraw NatSpec (RobotMoneyVault.sol:1091-1094) also carries no order warning.

refuted_candidates.title: The evidence secret scan still misses prefixed *_TOKEN names, including GITHUB_TOKEN and GH_TOKEN, which every gated 8453 run must have in its environment
refuted_candidates.reason: The regex gap is real, but no step of the leak path happens. Running bun against the shipped regex at publish-contracts/src/evidence-check.ts:1487 confirms that GITHUB_TOKEN=..., GH_TOKEN=..., "github_token": ... and NPM_TOKEN=... are not flagged, while TOKEN=... and CHAIN_SIGNER_PASSWORD=... are. The scenario still fails at every step that would put the token in the evidence folder. (1) Core's config check never receives the token. coreCheckEnv (publish-contracts/src/core-config-check.ts:25-30) passes only PATH, HOME and CONFIG_CHECK_RPC_URL to that child. (2) forge and cast are started directly with Bun.spawn (publish-contracts/src/runner.ts:59), not through a shell. Nothing in the repo uses set -x, and forge does not print its environment. Every forge failure tail that goes into an error is cleaned by scrubToolOutput with outputSecrets(ctx) (runner.ts:376-380, 388-390, 411; used at 700, 736, 911, 955 and redeploy-vault.ts:588, 620). outputSecrets collects the value of every baseEnv variable whose name matches /TOKEN/i and is at least 8 characters long. baseEnv is process.env (cli.ts:494, 560), so a GITHUB_TOKEN value becomes [redacted] before it reaches any error. (3) check-sha-green, the one child the release gate hands the token to (release-gate.ts:193-199), uses it only as an Authorization header (scripts/ci/check-sha-green.ts:138). Its error lines print only the URL and HTTP status (142, 192). (4) The JSON log is not written to the evidence directory. jsonLogger writes to process.stderr (publish-contracts/src/safe/log.ts:23), and run.failed is logged there (cli.ts:742). The run manifest has no error, output or stderr field. The evidence files the CLI writes are the manifest, adopted libraries, Safe manifests, the isomorphism report and core's config-check report (runner.ts:192, 1083, 1128; cli.ts:736), and none of them carry child stderr. No doc or workflow here sends publish stderr into the evidence folder. That leaves a defense-in-depth gap in a backstop scanner with no reachable leak path in this code.

clean_areas: [round 3] Lending adapter venue-refusal path (AaveV3Adapter/CompoundV3Adapter/MorphoAdapter deploy try/catch): the refused USDC goes back to VAULT, the allowance is always reset, a revert leaves no partial state, the Morpho exposure check stays outside the try, and the min-out overloads have no in-tree caller

[round 3] VaultAdapterOps._allocate measures by balance delta: no underflow, a refusal returns placed=0, and an over-return stays idle. The pass-1/pass-2 refused bitmask and cache invalidation (useCache requires refused==0) are consistent

[round 3] _ceiling vs MorphoAdapter._checkExposure: same expression (convertToAssets(balanceOf)) in the same block, so routing never asks past maxExposure. The staticcall tolerates adapters without the view

It acts only on an inactive index with an open record, clamps to the reported balance, credits by balance delta (an untrusted adapter cannot take idle), and finalizes only when the adapter reports empty.
